newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mixed after USDA report.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mixed after USDA report.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended mixed, with deferred months gaining on spillover support from CBOT and KCBT wheat after USDA's bullish winter wheat seedings report, traders said.
But while deferreds gained, nearby March drew pressure from stiff commercial selling and from ideas that Friday's crop report was bearish for old crop wheat.

New crop contracts in Kansas City and Chicago gained sharply after USDA estimated winter wheat seedings for the 1997 crop at 48.22 million acres, well below the average projection in the Reuter analysts survey of 51.40 million.
But USDA also raised its estimate of wheat end stocks, to 469 million bushels from its previous estimate of 435 million, and that pressured the market's front end.
"We opened higher with the other markets, but really there's not that much excitement in here because the report was for winter wheat," a MGE trader said at the midsession.
Local brokers bought the market on the way up, but large-scale commercial-related selling entered the market when the March contract neared $4.00 per bushel.
MGE spring wheat closed 1-1/2 cent per bushel lower to 6-1/2 cents higher, with March down 1-1/2 cents at $3.88-3/4. Earlier, March had climbed as high as $3.99-1/2.
Major players included Atwood-Peavey, which sold two million March and one million May. CIS, Wilson and LFG each bought at least one million March.
